fullPassage: In 2012, the Yale School of Architecture held a symposium called "Is Drawing Dead?" The bold title reflects a growing sense that the architect's freehand sketch is being displaced by the computer. The transition from sketchpad to screen entails, many architects believe, a loss of creativity, of adventurousness. Thanks to the precision and apparent completeness of screen renderings, a designer working at a computer has a tendency to lock in, visually and cognitively, on a design at an early stage. He bypasses much of the reflective and exploratory playfulness that springs from the uncertainty and ambiguity of sketching. Researchers term this phenomenon "premature fixation" and trace its cause to "the disincentive for design changes once a large amount of detail and interconnectedness is built too quickly into a CAD (Computer-Aided Design) model." The designer at the computer also tends to emphasize formal experimentation at the expense of expressiveness. By weakening an architect's "personal, emotional connection with the work," a renowned American architect and designer Michael Graves argues, CAD software produces designs that, "while complex and interesting in their own way," often "lack the emotional content of a design derived from hand."

ch: 예일 건축대학은 2012년에 컴퓨터 디자인의 장점을 홍보하는 행사를 개최했다.
스케치의 정밀성 덕분에 디자이너는 다양한 탐구적 실험을 할 수 있다.
Michael Graves는 CAD 소프트웨어가 감정적으로 풍부한 디자인을 생산한다고 주장했다.
컴퓨터로 작업하는 디자이너는 초기 단계에서 하나의 디자인에 고착되는 경향이 있다.

questions.passage: In 2012, the Yale School of Architecture held a symposium called "Is Drawing Dead?" The bold title reflects a growing sense that the architect's freehand sketch is being displaced by the computer. The transition from sketchpad to screen entails, many architects believe, a loss of creativity, of adventurousness. Thanks to the precision and apparent completeness of screen renderings, a designer working at a computer has a tendency to lock in, visually and cognitively, on a design at an early stage. He bypasses much of the reflective and exploratory playfulness that springs from the uncertainty and ambiguity of sketching. Researchers term this phenomenon "premature fixation" and trace its cause to "the disincentive for design changes once a large amount of detail and interconnectedness is built too quickly into a CAD (Computer-Aided Design) model." The designer at the computer also tends to emphasize formal experimentation at the expense of expressiveness. By weakening an architect's "personal, emotional connection with the work," a renowned American architect and designer Michael Graves argues, CAD software produces designs that, "while complex and interesting in their own way," often "lack the emotional content of a design derived from hand."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.analysis:
① 'The bold title reflects a growing sense that...freehand sketch is being displaced by the computer' → 일치

② 'Thanks to the precision and apparent completeness...has a tendency to lock in' → 일치

③ 'tends to emphasize formal experimentation at the expense of expressiveness' → 일치

④ 'detail and interconnectedness is built too quickly' → '빠르게' 구축될 때 disincentive 발생. '천천히'는 본문과 반대 ←정답
det.tip: too quickly(너무 빠르게) ≠ 천천히. 빠른 구축이 문제의 원인.

ch: 건축가의 손 스케치가 컴퓨터에 의해 대체되고 있다는 인식이 커지고 있다.
화면 렌더링의 정밀성과 완전성이 디자이너의 조기 고착에 기여한다.
컴퓨터 디자이너는 표현력을 희생하면서 형식적 실험을 강조하는 경향이 있다.
CAD 모델에 세부사항을 천천히 구축하면 디자인 변경 동기가 저하된다.
